violations.text: Raw animal foods were not stored properly to prevent cross-contamination in the walk-in cooler. Except when combined as ingredients, different types of raw animal foods must be separated from each other during storage by using separate equipment or arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/03/2026

Various food items were observed held at 105-120 degrees Fahrenheit in the steam stable. Food was placed in steam table under 2 hours prior to inspection. Food reheated to above 165 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/03/2026

Sour cream was observed held at 55 degrees Fahrenheit in the ice bath. Food kept in ice bath less than 2 hours prior to inspection. Food moved to walk-in cooler to rapidly cool. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/03/2026

The non-food contact surfaces of the ice machine have an accumulation of black residue. The ice machine must be cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the contamination of ice. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/03/2026

Homemade risotto that was made and date marked from over 7 days ago was observed in the walk-in cooler. Items prepared and cooked on-site must be used within 7 days. Person in charge voluntarily disposed of food at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 04/29/2025
The non-food contact surfaces of the ice machine has an accumulation of biofilm. New Violation. Correct By: 04/29/2025
The gasket of the prep unit was observed to be frayed. New Violation. Correct By: 03/19/2024
